name: Joseph E. Michaelis
title: Associate Professor
department: Computer Science; Learning + Interest + Technology Lab
fitReason: Applied AI/HRI fit in context-sensitive assistance, multimodal perception and model-mediated social interaction. His research emphasis is human-centered system design and learning sciences, rather than low-level robot-learning theory; a software/perception evaluation project would need explicit scoping.

physicalEvidence.summary: The complete 2026 Designing Robots for Families paper implements YOLO11 object/person detection and GPT-4.1 scene analysis on a real Temi mobile robot, with Raspberry Pi5 scheduling, custom Android/API commands and GPT-4.1-mini dialogue. Perception determines whether to deliver reminders or act in another location; navigation uses the platform’s existing stack rather than a newly learned navigation policy. Ten families co-designed the system, but two withdrew before deployment, leaving eight for approximately four-day autonomous home trials. Michaelis is a UIC coauthor on this Wisconsin-led collaboration; hardware access at UIC is not inferred. His separate 66-person 2026 Misty collaboration study explicitly uses Wizard-of-Oz, so it is not counted as autonomous learned execution.

shortVisit.summary: The current LIT Lab website and roster show an active independent group with graduate and undergraduate researchers and a past MS student, but no explicit current external-master summer invitation. A local degree roster is not a visiting research offer; eight-week compatibility, funding, remote participation and 2027 mentor capacity remain unknown.

unknowns: Current official UIC profile says Associate Professor; older personal lab biography says Assistant Professor. Use the current departmental title.
The Temi study is a multi-institution collaboration, and first-author institution is Wisconsin. It does not establish UIC ownership or access to that platform.

Reuse the existing UIC review: eligible overseas-degree Student Intern and scholar processes exist, but OIS must determine the actual category and host appointment. Published personal-funds documentation is not mentor acceptance.
The reviewed UIC scholar support threshold is $2,400/month and processing guidance is roughly 60 days from OIS receipt; verify applicable student-intern amounts, insurance, fees and 2027 terms.
Family/child-participant research and data access require independent ethics and safeguarding approval. No clinical efficacy or unrestricted visitor access follows from this study.
No all-10-family deployment or autonomous Misty claim should be made; complete methods distinguish these study designs.
Public robot research does not confirm current equipment access, a summer 2027 offer or host availability.
